questions.stem: A train travels in a straight line along a road covering a distance of $$ 45 \text{ km} $$ in $$ 15 \text{ minutes} $$. What is its average velocity, in $$ \text{km/h} $$?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify given values.**
Distance ($$ d $$) = $$ 45 \text{ km} $$
Time ($$ t $$) = $$ 15 \text{ minutes} $$

**Step 2: Convert time to hours.**
$$ t = \frac{15}{60} \text{ hours} = 0.25 \text{ h} $$

**Step 3: Apply the average velocity formula.**
$$ V_{avg} = \frac{d}{t} $$
$$ V_{avg} = \frac{45 \text{ km}}{0.25 \text{ h}} = 180 \text{ km/h} $$

**Result:** 180 km/h

similar_questions.stem: A teacher with a motorbike travelled 40 km for 1 h along a straight road. He took 20 min rest and again travelled 20 km for 2 h along the same straight road. The teacher's average speed, in km/h, is
explanation_steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time taken (G9 p.72–73).
Total distance = 40 km + 20 km = 60 km.
Total time = 1 h + 20 min + 2 h = 3 h 20 min = 3⅓ h (the rest time counts – the clock keeps running).
Average speed = 60 ÷ 3.333 = 18 km/h. Answer: B. (Ignoring the rest gives 60 ÷ 3 = 20 km/h – option C, a common trap.)

explanation_steps: Relative velocity: v(truck relative to bus) = v(truck) − v(bus) (G10 p.19–23).
Take west as positive: v(truck) = +65 km/h, v(bus) = −45 km/h (east).
v(truck rel. bus) = 65 − (−45) = +110 km/h, i.e. 110 km/h towards the west. Answer: A.

The system is heated and its temperature rises to $120 ^\circ\text{C}$ as the steam expands to a volume of $230 \text{ cm}^3$ at a constant pressure of $5 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$. Calculate
(a) the work done by the steam.
(b) the change in its internal energy.
explanation_steps:
**Given:**
$m = 100 \text{ g} = 0.1 \text{ kg}$
$V_1 = 200 \text{ cm}^3 = 200 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^3$
$V_2 = 230 \text{ cm}^3 = 230 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^3$
$P = 5 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$
$c_{steam} = 2.02 \times 10^3 \text{ J/kg}\cdot\text{K}$ (from constants)
$\Delta T = 120 - 100 = 20 \text{ K}$

**(a) Work Done:**
$W = P \times \Delta V = P(V_2 - V_1)$
$W = 5 \times 10^5 \times (230 - 200) \times 10^{-6}$
$W = 5 \times 10^5 \times 30 \times 10^{-6} = 15 \text{ J}$

**(b) Internal Energy Change:**
First, find heat added ($Q$):
$Q = mc\Delta T = 0.1 \times 2020 \times 20 = 4040 \text{ J}$
Using 1st Law: $\Delta U = Q - W$
$\Delta U = 4040 - 15 = 4025 \text{ J}$

A student in a laboratory stretches a spring $0.5 \text{ m}$ from rest by exerting a force which increases uniformly from zero to $250 \text{ N}$. Find the
(a) equivalent spring constant of the system.
(b) work done by the student in pulling the spring.
explanation_steps:

$x = 0.5 \text{ m}$, $F_{max} = 250 \text{ N}$

**(a) Spring Constant:**

$k = 250 / 0.5 = 500 \text{ N/m}$

$W = \frac{1}{2}(500)(0.5)^2 = 250 \times 0.25 = 62.5 \text{ J}$

Ray of light travelling with frequency of $$ 10^{15} \, Hz $$ in air strikes a glass surface (n=1.2) at $$ 53^\circ $$ with the surface. 
A) What is the angle of refraction?
B) What is the wavelength of the light in glass?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Find Angle of Incidence (i).**
The angle with the surface is $$ 53^\circ $$, so the angle with the normal is:
$$ i = 90^\circ - 53^\circ = 37^\circ $$

**Step 2: Find Angle of Refraction (r) using Snell's Law.**
$$ n_1 \sin i = n_2 \sin r $$
$$ 1 \times \sin 37^\circ = 1.2 \times \sin r $$
$$ 0.6 = 1.2 \sin r \Rightarrow \sin r = 0.5 \Rightarrow r = 30^\circ $$

**Step 3: Find Wavelength in glass ($$ \lambda_g $$).**
Speed in glass $$ v = \frac{c}{n} = \frac{3 \times 10^8}{1.2} = 2.5 \times 10^8 \, m/s $$
$$ \lambda_g = \frac{v}{f} = \frac{2.5 \times 10^8}{10^{15}} = 2.5 \times 10^{-7} \, m = 250 \, nm $$

(a) Calculate the energy of a photon whose wavelength is $1.32 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$.
(b) Ultraviolet radiation of $7.2 \text{ eV}$ energy falls on an aluminum surface of $4.2 \text{ eV}$ work function. Find the kinetic energy, in joules, of the fastest electrons emitted.
explanation_steps:
**(a) Photon Energy:**
$E = hc / \lambda$
$E = (6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8) / (1.32 \times 10^{-10})$
$E = (19.8 \times 10^{-26}) / (1.32 \times 10^{-10}) = 15 \times 10^{-16} = 1.5 \times 10^{-15} \text{ J}$

**(b) Kinetic Energy:**
Einstein's equation: $K_{max} = E_{photon} - \Phi$
$K_{max} = 7.2 \text{ eV} - 4.2 \text{ eV} = 3.0 \text{ eV}$
Convert to Joules:
$K_{max} = 3.0 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = 4.8 \times 10^{-19} \text{ J}$

a) Threshold frequency
b) Kinetic energy in ev
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate Threshold Frequency ($$ f_0 $$).**
$$ \Phi = h f_0 \implies f_0 = \frac{\Phi}{h} $$
Convert $$ \Phi $$ to Joules: $$ 2.46 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = 3.936 \times 10^{-19} J $$.
$$ f_0 = \frac{3.936 \times 10^{-19}}{6.63 \times 10^{-34}} \approx 5.94 \times 10^{14} Hz $$.

**Step 2: Calculate Photon Energy ($$ E $$).**
$$ E = \frac{hc}{\lambda} = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{300 \times 10^{-9}} = 6.63 \times 10^{-19} J $$.
Convert to eV: $$ \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-19}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}} \approx 4.14 eV $$.

**Step 3: Calculate Kinetic Energy ($$ K.E. $$).**
$$ K.E. = E - \Phi = 4.14 eV - 2.46 eV = 1.68 eV $$.
